egress.terms: no traffic allowance is published; the rules name only abuse as a reason for blocking; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: configuration help pages plus a broker panel; no API described
tooling: a 6in4 interface on Linux or a router; the site publishes configuration help
chaining: needs a public IPv4, so it fits a free VM with an IPv4 address.
binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary is published: free, no byte meter, no rate. The gate is a public IPv4 for 6in4 and the non-commercial scope stated in the rules; neither is a volume constraint, so nothing fails at 1 TiB/month.

identity_cost.detail: a registration on the broker site is required; the field list was not read

reliability_note: the rules reserve the right to block without warning for hacking or spam.
confidence_note: the free price and the private non-commercial scope are documented from the vendor's rules page; the /48 size comes from the search engine's indexed text of the broker page, because the page as extracted returned only the introductory article. Reading the broker page through a browser session would raise it.

the service is described as 6in4, encapsulating IPv6 in IPv4
